To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
exposure of mammalian cells to ionizing radiation results in down-regulation of genes encoding cyclin B, cdc2, and cdc 25.

the down-regulations of cdc2, cdc25, cyclin A and cyclin B gene expression following exposure to ionizing radiation are at least in part mediated through a decrease in RNA stability and that these effects may play a role in the lethality induced by ionizing radiation.
ionizing radiation causes transient down-regulation in the expression of cdc2, cdc25, cyclin A and cyclin B. This down-regulation is at least in some cases due to a decrease RNA stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms responsible for the effects of ionization radiation on cell cycle control gene regulation.
understanding how ionizing radiation induces growth arrest, DNA damage, and lethality in mammalian cells.
the effects of ionization radiation on the expression and regulation of genes involved in the control of cell proliferation.
